author: Eyton, 1838

art.subject: Redhead (Aythya americana), adult male in winter: rounded head and upper neck bright chestnut-red; lower neck and breast black; back and flanks medium grey, finely vermiculated; rear end and undertail black; belly white. Bill pale bluish grey with a narrow whitish band near the tip and a black tip; bright yellow eye; grey legs.
art.pose: swimming on open water, side view, head held up
art.scene: Korean winter reservoir with calm open water and dry reed edges; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Medium-sized, compact diving duck, a little larger than the Common Pochard, sitting low on the water. Head rounded with a steep forehead, not a long sloping wedge. Bill medium length, a little shorter than the head, broad and fairly straight along the top. Legs short, set far back. Tail short, held flat on the water. In flight a grey upperwing with a paler grey stripe along the flight feathers. Female plain warm brown with a paler face, a pale eye-ring, dark eye and a grey bill with a pale band and dark tip.
avoid: Do not paint a sloping forehead, a long black bill with a grey band or a red eye; those mark the Common Pochard (Aythya ferina).
Do not make the back and flanks whitish with a long wedge-shaped head and black bill (Canvasback).
Do not paint a white wing stripe like the Tufted Duck; the wing stripe is pale grey.
